skill.name: git-advanced
skill.description: Advanced Git workflow guidance for interactive rebase, conflict resolution, bisect debugging, branch strategy, history cleanup, and reflog recovery.
skill.summary: Plan and execute advanced Git workflows with safety checks and recovery guidance.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Git examples, Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, and standard troubleshooting commands. I found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized network behavior. The skill includes workflows and a Bash helper that can modify repository history, so users should review commands and keep backups.

remediation.issue: Destructive Git workflows appear in documentation and the helper script.
remediation.suggestion: Keep safety warnings next to reset, clean, branch deletion, stash clearing, and history rewrite steps.

remediation.issue: The helper script accepts some interactive values with limited validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate stash numbers, branch names, and destructive selections before running Git commands.

remediation.issue: SSH private key troubleshooting appears in the documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that ssh-add reads a local key only and must never print, copy, or upload private key material.

static_findings.snippet: Follow these best practices to maintain clean Git history, avoid common pitfalls, and work effective
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v HEAD); do
git branch --merged | grep -v "\*\|main\|develop" | xargs -n 1 git branch -d
git branch --merged main | grep -v "^\*\|main\|develop" | xargs git branch -d
git branch | grep "feature/your-" | xargs git branch -d
git branch --merged main | grep -v "^\*\|main\|develop" | xargs git branch -d
# Rebase more frequently to avoid large divergence
for branch in $(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/); do
git branch --merged | grep -v "\*\|main\|master\|develop\|development" | xargs -r git branch -d
- `squash` (s): Combine with previous commit, keep message
- `fixup` (f): Combine with previous commit, discard message
- Use `git reflog` if something goes wrong

For common conflict patterns and solutions, see `examples/conflict_resolution.md`.

- `scripts/git_helper.sh`: Branch cleanup and conflict resolution utilities

content.value_statement: Complex Git history can be hard to repair without losing work. This skill provides guided workflows for rebase, conflicts, bisect, recovery, and branch management.
actual_capabilities: Guides interactive rebase workflows, including squash, reword, edit, split, and drop.
Explains merge conflict markers and ours/theirs choices.
Provides Git bisect steps for manual and automated regression searches.
Covers reflog recovery for deleted branches, bad resets, and lost commits.
Includes a Bash helper script for branch cleanup, conflict resolution, history viewing, and stash management.
Compares Git Flow, trunk-based development, and feature branch strategies.
limitations: Requires the user to review and run Git commands in the target repository.
Some workflows can rewrite history or delete local data if used incorrectly.
Does not connect to hosted Git providers or inspect remote permissions.
The helper script assumes a Unix-like shell and Git command-line tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Clean a feature branch, squash noisy commits, and create a reviewable history before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Recover Repository State
use_cases.description: Use reflog, backup branches, and reset guidance to recover from deleted branches or bad history changes.

use_cases.title: Manage Team Branching
use_cases.description: Choose a branch strategy, define release flows, and clean stale branches with safer review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Clean My Branch History
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review my recent commits and plan a safe interactive rebase before opening a pull request. Ask before suggesting destructive commands.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Merge Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through resolving conflicts between my branch and main. Explain when to use ours, theirs, or a manual merge.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Regression with Bisect
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Git bisect plan for a regression. Help me choose good and bad commits, test steps, and reset instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Branch Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Git Flow, trunk-based, and GitHub Flow for my team. Include release, hotfix, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: I have five messy commits and want a clean pull request.
output_examples.output: A rebase plan that backs up the branch, groups related changes, improves commit messages, and explains when force-with-lease is appropriate.

output_examples.input: My merge has conflicts in configuration and tests.
output_examples.output: A conflict checklist that compares both sides, recommends manual integration, stages resolved files, and verifies the result with tests.

output_examples.input: A bug appeared sometime during the last month.
output_examples.output: A bisect workflow with known good and bad points, repeatable test guidance, and cleanup steps after the search finishes.

best_practices: Create a backup branch before rebasing, resetting, or filtering history.
Prefer force-with-lease and team coordination when rewriting pushed commits.
Run tests and inspect diffs after resolving conflicts or applying recovery steps.
anti_patterns: Running destructive Git commands without checking the current branch and working tree.
Accepting all ours or all theirs in conflicts without reading the changes.
Force pushing shared branches without review or team coordination.

faq.question: Can this skill run Git commands for me?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance and includes a helper script. You should review every command before running it.

faq.question: Is it safe to rewrite Git history?
faq.answer: History rewriting can be safe on private branches with backups. Coordinate before changing shared history.

faq.question: Does the skill support merge conflict resolution?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains conflict markers, ours and theirs choices, manual merges, and verification steps.

faq.question: Can it help recover deleted commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers reflog recovery, backup branches, lost commit recovery, and undoing bad resets.

faq.question: Does it require a specific Git hosting provider?
faq.answer: No. The guidance uses local Git commands and works with most providers.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers and maintainers who already know basic Git and need help with advanced workflows.
